findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, meaning the RDS instance data at rest is not encrypted, exposing sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the MySQL database instance directly to the internet, significantly increasing the attack surface.
The database uses a plaintext password variable (var.password) and default admin username, with the password also passed in plaintext through EC2 user data, increasing risk of credential leakage.
Egress rule allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports and protocols, which is overly permissive and could facilitate data exfiltration if the instance or DB is compromised.

The IAM policy grants full wildcard permissions (s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) on all resources (Resource: "*"), violating least privilege and allowing the EC2 instance role to perform unrestricted actions across these services.
The EC2 instance's user_data script embeds the database password in plaintext (var.password), which is visible to anyone with access to the instance metadata or console, risking credential exposure.

findings.issue_category: disabled backup retention weakening recovery/security posture
findings.description: backup_retention_period is set to 0, disabling automated backups; combined with skip_final_snapshot = true, this could hinder forensic recovery in case of a security incident or data loss.
